top: Israel's president has picked Gadi Eisenkot, not Benjamin Netanyahu, to try to form the next government, after 67 of 120 MPs backed him.
Wall Street bounced on Friday after its AI rout, helped by a strong US jobs report, but the ASX still slipped 0.5% to 9,020.8.
Wall Street had its worst day since April 2025, with the Nasdaq sliding into correction as AI and chip stocks were hit by fears of tougher regulation after the Democrats' midterm sweep.
The RBA lifted the cash rate to 4.85%, the highest since 2008, in a split 6 to 3 vote that hints at a pause.
Israel's president starts coalition talks on Wednesday after an election that gave neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot a majority.
Alphabet's slide has now wiped roughly half a trillion US dollars off its value, and Amazon's mixed results kept Wall Street nervous about the cost of AI.
Israel's vote count is done at 99.9 percent and still gives Netanyahu's bloc only 53 of 120 seats, with the Arab parties on 19 and holding the key.
Australian inflation hit 4.3% in September, which makes an RBA rate rise on Melbourne Cup Day (3 November) close to a sure thing.
Israel's election has ended without a clear winner, with exit polls showing neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition reaching a 61 seat majority.
Israelis vote today in an election that polls say could leave neither side with a majority.
Lula has won a record fourth term as Brazil's president, but Flávio Bolsonaro is refusing to concede and plans to challenge the result.
Brazil picks its president today in a runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro that polls call a coin flip.
